title: The OSI Model
markdown:
Established in 1947, the **International Organization for Standardization (ISO)** is a multinational body dedicated to global agreement on international standards.

An ISO standard that covers all aspects of network communications is the **Open Systems Interconnection (OSI)** model, first introduced in the late 1970s.

> **ISO vs. OSI**: **ISO** is the organization; **OSI** is the model.

### Why a Layered Architecture?

Computer networks are complex systems. Partitioning communication functions into a hierarchical stack of layers provides significant benefits:

1. **Modularity** — A complex problem is divided into smaller, well-defined pieces.
2. **Independent Development** — Each layer can be updated or replaced without affecting adjacent layers.
3. **Standard Interfaces** — Adjacent layers communicate through clearly defined interfaces.
4. **Interoperability** — Systems from different vendors can communicate if they adhere to the same layer standards.
